digest.component_or_area: test suite: subprocess and network timeouts
propositions: Real-subprocess reap tests depend on implicit wall-clock ordering where child setup completes before injected timeouts fire; this ordering is fragile under load and must be made explicit via readiness gates.

Module-wide blanket autouse timeout fixture creates a latent load flake: reap tests need short windows to ensure timeouts fire, but the 429-retry test needs a long window for two sequential spawns to complete.
Snapshot stall-window fixture injects a 2s low-speed delay but sibling dribble test already proved a 1s window is sufficient and honored by git.
Split blanket fixture into opt-in reap-timing fixture (0.2s call/0.1s grace/0.1s drain) and completing-child timeout fixture (30s), eliminating the dual-constraint conflict.

Add explicit readiness gates via file markers in fake children and parent-side polling wrappers, so child-setup races are ordered before deadline measurement rather than relying on elapsed-time margins.
Reduce stall-window from 2s to 1s while keeping throughput-keyed pass condition and unchanged 60s ceiling, so test latency degrades gracefully under load but does not flake.
